layers.description: The USGS Transportation downloadable data from The National Map (TNM) includes railroad features sourced from the Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) National Rail Network. Transportation data consists of active and inactive rail lines, rail yards, and related infrastructure associated with the transport of people or freight. The data include the name, ownership, classification, subdivision, and location of rail features. Railroad data support general mapping and geographic information system technology analysis for applications such as hazardous materials routing, emergency response planning, and infrastructure management.

columns.name: fid
columns.description: The unique integer identifier assigned to each feature in the dataset.

columns.name: fcode
columns.description: The USGS National Map feature code that classifies the type of rail feature. Feature codes follow the USGS Feature Class Code (FCC) standard and indicate the specific category of transportation infrastructure.

columns.name: name
columns.description: The official or common name of the rail line or feature, as attributed by the source dataset. May include the railroad company name or the name of the route.

columns.name: rail_class
columns.description: The Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) classification of the railroad, indicating the size and revenue level of the carrier. Class I railroads are the largest by revenue; Class II and III are regional and local carriers respectively.

columns.name: rail_owner
columns.description: The name of the organization or company that owns the rail line or infrastructure, as reported in the source dataset.

columns.name: rail_owner_code
columns.description: The abbreviated code (typically 2–4 characters) identifying the railroad owner, following the Association of American Railroads (AAR) or Surface Transportation Board (STB) reporting mark conventions.

columns.name: rail_subdiv
columns.description: The name of the railroad subdivision, which is an operational segment or district used by the railroad company to organize and manage its network. Subdivisions often reflect historical acquisition or operational boundaries.

columns.name: rail_usage
columns.description: A description of the current operational usage of the rail line, such as mainline, branch line, yard lead, or abandoned. May contain multiple values separated by commas if the segment serves more than one purpose.

columns.name: length_km
columns.description: The calculated length of the rail feature in kilometers, as computed from the geometry of the feature in the source dataset.

columns.name: load_date
columns.description: The date the feature was loaded into The National Map database, formatted as an ISO 8601 datetime string. Useful for tracking data currency and identifying recently updated features.

columns.name: permanent_id
columns.description: A stable, globally unique identifier assigned to the feature by USGS for long-term tracking across dataset versions and updates. This identifier persists even when feature attributes are revised.

columns.name: source_dataset
columns.description: A brief narrative identifying the source dataset from which the rail feature was derived, such as the FRA National Rail Network or another authoritative transportation data source.

columns.name: source_dataset_date
columns.description: The date or version of the source dataset from which the feature was derived, helping to document the currency and lineage of the data.

columns.name: source_feature_id
columns.description: The unique identifier of the feature in the original source dataset, allowing cross-referencing back to the authoritative source for verification or additional attribute lookup.

columns.name: source_originator
columns.description: The organization or agency responsible for creating or maintaining the original source dataset, such as the Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) or U.S. Census Bureau.
